title: District VIII Voters Face Two Elections on Two Saturdays in December
excerpt: Voters in Laredo’s District VIII will head to the polls on two different Saturdays in December — Dec. 5 for a special election to fill the District VIII council seat, and Dec. 12 for the mayoral runoff — with separate early-voting windows for each, and a dispute over polling places still unresolved.
content:
Voters in Laredo’s District VIII will head to the polls on two different Saturdays in December — Dec. 5 for a special election to fill the District VIII council seat, and Dec. 12 for the mayoral runoff — with separate early-voting windows for each, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The Dec. 5 special election will choose the City Council member for District VIII, under a city resolution ordering the vote. Early voting for that election runs Nov. 23 through Dec. 1, closed Nov. 26 and 27, with the main early-voting site at the Webb County Elections Office, 720 Convent Ave. Polls will be open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on election day, according to the resolution.

The Dec. 12 ballot carries the mayoral runoff between District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa, who led the Nov. 3 vote with 35.10 percent, and incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, who finished second with 32.5 percent, according to KGNS. Early voting for the mayoral runoff runs Nov. 30 through Dec. 8, according to KGNS. The Laredo College Board of Trustees Position 9 runoff, between Tita Vela and Dr. Eduardo Lopez, is also set for Dec. 12, with early voting Nov. 30 through Dec. 5.

On top of the two dates, a dispute over where District 8 voters can cast ballots remains unresolved. At a City Hall meeting Monday, Nov. 16, a request to add the Marcos Aranda Recreation Center as a polling site ended in a stalemate, with no vote taken before a state-mandated deadline forced the meeting to adjourn at 11 p.m., according to KGNS.

Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa, who requested the added site, called the situation a failure of management, according to KGNS. Councilwoman Melissa Cigarroa said: “To purposefully close down a site in a district where it gets the highest vote totals is fundamentally unfair and undemocratic.”

The only other west-side option is the Webb County Elections Office, which is frequently blocked by passing trains, according to KGNS. City officials said they were unable to make changes because the Secretary of State was blocking modifications once early voting begins Nov. 23.

The City Council approved the Dec. 12 runoff plan on Nov. 13, including an estimated $97,475.17 contract with the Webb County Elections Office.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 18, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026; City of Laredo Resolution 2026-R-205; KGNS, Nov. 4, 2026.
